meta.note: Educational comparison, not a prediction and not an official evacuation plan. Street-segment level only; no parcels or addresses. Coordinates in local meters (network.json crs).
meta.crs: EPSG:32610 local: x = easting - xmin, y = northing - ymin (meters)

provenance.graph: derived: data/model/network.json drivable edges as js/sim.js builds links (vehicle mode, not disconnected, not closed by a barrier; one arc per direction with lanes)
provenance.exits: model rule: net.meta.exitNodes, streets cut at the edge of the elevation grid
provenance.chokeEdges: derived: the entrance choke, edge dominators of the reversed graph rooted at the exits; arcs in series through a node with two drivable streets form one entrance
provenance.stemChokeEdges: derived: every choke arc on the same dead-end stem (model rule: a choke whose outer end has a single way out joins the area above it)
provenance.type: derived: "dead end" if every entrance edge is a bridge of the undirected drivable network, else "one-way" (one-way directions from the County TRVLWAY field and OSM oneway tags)
provenance.nesting: derived: number of areas in series between the area and an exit, its own included (model rule: a loop of under 200 m of street does not start a new area)
provenance.residents: synthetic: zone population inside the model area (Genasys, or the 2020 Census where data/assumptions.json population.overrides or a missing estimate says so) spread over street length as js/sim.js does (Principal Arterials weighted 0.7; no freeways or ramps); expected values
provenance.households: assumption: residents / 2.37 persons per household (data/assumptions.json demand)
provenance.vehicles: assumption: households × (1 − 0.0747) × 1.208 vehicles taken (Time Study Fig. D-11 shares, data/assumptions.json demand)
provenance.narrowestStemChoke: derived: narrowest choke edge on the stem, same parking state; residentsBehind counts residents on streets from which every route to every exit crosses it (the edge itself included)
provenance.residentsBehindEngineBlockedChoke: derived: residents on streets from which every route to every exit crosses a choke edge under access.engineClearM (10 ft) of clear width, this area's or one further out
provenance.choke: derived: narrowest entrance edge under status-quo parking in its nominal state (js/parking.js, seed null: both sides where they fit, perfect parking); engine fits if clear width ≥ access.engineClearM (10 ft); fire-code width 20 ft; tiers from the SB 99 report p. 4
provenance.steepestGradePct: derived: largest 25 m-window grade (gradeMax, DEM) on any street in the area, unreliable segments left out
provenance.nearestOtherStreet: derived: shortest straight line from the area streets (sampled every 10 m) to a drivable street outside the area (no freeways or ramps) where driving from the area point to the outside point now, along legal one-way directions, takes at least 300 m and 3 times the line (model rule); climb from the DEM. A hint, not a route or a design
provenance.nearestFreeStreet: derived: same, to a street behind no choke point
provenance.existingLink: derived: shortest chain of path, stairway, no-vehicle (County TRVLWAY NT) or barrier-closed segments from the area to a drivable street outside it (search limit 1.5 km)
provenance.emergencyVehicleLink: derived: same, through barrier-closed vehicle segments only (diverters, bollards, gates); enginesPass from OSM emergency=yes
provenance.constraint: model rule: score = residents × nesting × narrowFactor × hillFactor; narrowFactor 4/3/2/1 for SB 99 tiers severely (≤ 6 ft) / moderately (7–8 ft) / constrained (9–10 ft) / not narrow, unknown width 1; hillFactor = 1 + share of residents on Fire Zone 2–3 streets

sb99.source: SB 99 Access Impaired Neighborhood Analysis, KLD TR-1380 Rev. 3 (2024-02-19), Table 1, primary AINs; parsed from data/raw/docs/sb99.txt
